_comment: Hand-authored. export_data.py never touches this file.
Deciding whether something belongs under People or Places is a judgement, so it
is written down here rather than guessed from the workbook. Every id in a
'studies' list must exist in studies.json - check_publish.py verifies that.
Keyed by topic id from data/topics.json, which is where the title, heading and
question for each topic live - not repeated here, so there is one place to edit.
'name' is no longer drawn on screen. A card is titled by the reference of each
source it cites, because a summary sitting where a title sits reads as though it
were the name of a source. Keep it as the editorial label for whoever edits this
file; 'note' is what the reader sees under the title.

health-system.intro: Every card comes from published sources: an action with evidence behind it, or a measure already defined.

people-actions.name: Prevention delivered to individuals, with a return on investment attached
people-actions.note: Programmes aimed at particular people - screening, counselling, vaccination - with a costed return. Across the published studies the median return was 14 dollars back for every dollar spent.

people-actions.name: Best-buy interventions for chronic disease
people-actions.note: The World Health Organization's shortlist of prevention measures for heart disease, cancer and diabetes, each with a modelled return.

people-actions.name: A ranked list of 123 preventive interventions by value for money
people-actions.note: An Australian exercise, led by the University of Queensland, that put preventive measures in order of cost per healthy year of life gained. The nearest thing to a priority funding menu.

people-measures.name: Preventable hospitalisation rate, split by age and sex
people-measures.note: The standard national indicator, already published broken down by sex and by age group. Downloadable now, seven years of it.

people-measures.name: Preventable admissions set against a person's own circumstances
people-measures.note: Smoking, physical activity, body mass index, income and education linked to whether that person was later admitted. Needs an application to the data custodians.

people-measures.name: Healthy years of life gained per person
people-measures.note: The common currency for comparing very different interventions. Used in both the Australian and the English costing work.

places-actions.name: Population-wide measures such as taxes and regulation
places-actions.note: In the Australian ranking these came out strongest - they change the environment for everyone rather than one person at a time.

places-actions.name: National delivery against local delivery
places-actions.note: Worth knowing before designing anything: the same review found local interventions returned 4.1 to 1 while national ones returned 27.2 to 1.

places-actions.name: Programmes intended to avoid hospital admissions
places-actions.note: A review that grades the evidence rather than assuming it. Several widely used approaches turn out to have weak support.

places-actions.name: A caution before comparing one area with another
places-actions.note: A worse area result mostly reflects the resident population rather than local service performance. General practitioner supply explained 2.9 per cent of the difference between areas; people's own circumstances explained 36.9 per cent.

places-measures.name: Preventable hospitalisation rate by area
places-measures.note: Published for 346 small areas, 33 primary health network regions, four remoteness categories and five socioeconomic groups. Not published by local government area or hospital and health service, which is a real gap.

places-measures.name: Service and population contributions to area gaps
places-measures.note: A method for splitting the difference between areas into the part explained by service supply and the part explained by resident population.

places-measures.name: Regional share and cost of preventable admissions
places-measures.note: The one study in this set that looks specifically at regional Queensland.

places-measures.name: Australia compared with other wealthy countries
places-measures.note: Avoidable admission rates for asthma, chronic lung disease, heart failure and diabetes, on a comparable basis across countries.
